test: Switchcraft 1.1.0 mixed UK/RU/EN input stress test
conclusions: Paused control: exact 3000-character match at 91.35 characters/second.
Correct mixed-language prose: exact match in balanced and careful modes.
At 29.22 characters/second and 80 ms word pauses: all 13 ordinary wrong-layout tokens corrected; the separately mutated URL correctly preserved.
At 88.53 characters/second and no word pauses: all 13 ordinary errors missed, original input preserved exactly.
No lost characters, unwanted word changes, harness exceptions, or hook-health failures in the validated five passes.

Replacement confirmation defect: 13 words changed in the actual normal-speed result, only 2 Corrected events; 11 unconfirmed-paste status messages. The production fallback leaves temporary correction text on the clipboard.
inferred_causes: KeyboardService Current requires an unchanged input sequence. At fast input, the next key can invalidate replacement before it starts.
After paste, confirmation also requires the same sequence; subsequent input can prevent confirmation despite successful insertion. Clipboard restoration depends on confirmation.
limitations: The native automation helper did not type into Notepad++; these 3000-character runs use a dedicated WPF editor and the production KeyboardService/NativeEngine classes.
Layout is explicitly selected per token; 14 typographic characters use isolated Unicode fallback. This is a finite generated sample, not a universal accuracy score.
Preliminary unsynchronized Unicode and virtual-key control attempts failed even with correction paused; they were retained separately and excluded from final product conclusions.
